subject.title: fix: persist pending followup queues across gateway restart

question: Should OpenClaw advance restart followup recovery through a SQLite-backed successor and treat this JSON-sidecar branch as source context, or intentionally sponsor this PR's sidecar and system-event replay approach?
rationale: The remaining blocker is a storage ownership and prompt-boundary decision that automation cannot safely settle, especially with a newer unmerged SQLite candidate.

options.title: Advance SQLite recovery
options.body: Use the newer SQLite-backed direction or a rebased successor after conflicts, context persistence, and exact-head transport proof are resolved.

options.title: Sponsor this sidecar branch
options.body: Maintainers can explicitly accept a JSON sidecar exception plus the replay semantics after requiring fixes for duplicate replay, staleness, and trust-boundary handling.

options.title: Pause behind broader queue API work
options.body: Wait for the broader followup/runtime API boundary if durable restart recovery should be solved through a new owner contract first.

recommendation.title: Advance SQLite recovery
recommendation.body: Use the newer SQLite-backed direction or a rebased successor after conflicts, context persistence, and exact-head transport proof are resolved.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest combined history on queue lifecycle, system-event authority, and gateway startup surfaces involved in this product/storage decision.
